note: Story shapes: how a video's beats are arranged (owner, 2026-10-30: every Short had '4 levels', which felt repetitive; the shapes must keep growing so no cycle forms). A plan names one in `shape` (generator/shapes.py), or invents a new one ({id, name, beats, why}), which ship adds here as `trial`. Every shape keeps the shared spine (generator/story.py): a curiosity hook, the promise early, rising stakes, a turn, a payoff that answers the hook. Only a shape with `levels: true` shows the level chips and a climbing counter. Research adds shapes it sees in top videos (with the reference); the improver promotes trial shapes that beat the median stayed-to-watch / % viewed, and retires ones that keep underperforming. Status: active | trial | retired.

shapes.name: Levels
shapes.when: only when the topic IS a ladder people wait to climb: levels of wealth, $100 to a strap to a pallet to a room, an hour to a decade
shapes.beats: hook -> promise the ladder ('four steps up') -> each level a beat, the counter climbing -> the turn at the top -> the payoff

shapes.name: The reveal (open loop and clues)
shapes.when: how a business really makes money, a secret of the rich, a billionaire question: there is one hidden answer
shapes.beats: hook: the surprising fact and the question, no answer -> promise ('here's how') -> clue one, clue two, clue three, each a bigger piece -> the turn (the piece nobody expects) -> the payoff answers the hook in one line

reference.title: Why does the casino always win, even when nobody cheats? | How Casinos Make Money

shapes.name: Versus
shapes.when: two people or two choices in the same situation, one difference that decides everything
shapes.beats: hook: the same moment, two outcomes -> promise ('one choice decides it') -> side by side: what each does, step by step, the gap widening -> the turn (the real reason) -> the payoff

reference.title: rich vs poor parents buying you a car

shapes.name: Countdown
shapes.when: a handful of things of one kind (tricks, traps, ways): number three, two, then the biggest
shapes.beats: hook: the biggest one teased, not shown -> promise ('three ways, the last is the worst') -> three, two -> the turn -> number one, the payoff

reference.title: 6 Ways Rich People Make Money With Debt

shapes.name: Before and after
shapes.when: one change and what it did: a decision, a law, a company's move, a fortune over time
shapes.beats: hook: the after, shocking, with the question how -> the before, in enough detail to matter -> the change -> what happened step by step -> the turn -> the payoff (the after, explained)

reference.title: Everyone Called Him an Idiot. He Got Richer Every Time.

shapes.name: Then and now
shapes.when: how something changed across years: a price, a fortune, an industry, who was the first billionaire of it
shapes.beats: hook: today's figure next to the old one, and why -> the start -> two or three moments that changed it, in order -> the turn -> today, explained

reference.title: Who Was The 1st Billionaire In These Industries?!

shapes.name: What if
shapes.when: an imagined scenario at a scale people can't picture: spend $1 trillion in a day, pay off the national debt, give everyone a billion
shapes.beats: hook: the wild question -> the rules of the game -> try it, step by step, the number growing -> the turn (where it breaks) -> the payoff (what it teaches)

reference.title: I Tried to Spend $1 TRILLION in One Day

shapes.name: The question chain (asker and explainer)
shapes.when: a billionaire or big-money mechanism with several layers: how the rich pay no tax, how a company really earns, why a famous person does something strange
shapes.beats: hook: the asker states the shocking fact and asks why -> the explainer answers in one line and one picture -> the asker's next, sharper question (doubt, then how, then a real example, then outrage, then 'and people like us?') -> each answer a real name and a figure, a named term on a card -> the named secret -> a 3-line recap, the lesson, the asker's last question to the viewer

reference.title: Why Billionaires Take $0 Salary… But Never Go Broke

shapes.name: The ladder parable (same start, different steps)
shapes.when: one money idea shown as people climbing it: same $100, four brothers; same salary, three friends. Each step a named finance term, the result multiplied at every step
shapes.beats: hook: the same start and the wildly different end -> the cast in a lineup -> person one: the simplest move, the sum built on screen from units, its term -> person two, three, four: each one more clever move, a small conflict (who pays if it fails?) and how it's solved, the sum and the term -> the bars side by side -> the 3-line contrast recap -> 'which one are you?'

reference.title: How $100 Became $204,984: The Egg Selling Mindset

shapes.name: The true rise (and the hits)
shapes.when: how a real company, person or place got rich: a founding sum, dated steps, a crisis, the comeback
shapes.beats: hook: the question written huge over today's picture ('why is X so rich?') -> rewind to the start with its date and sum -> growth you can count (stores, customers, ships) -> 'but then' the dated setbacks -> the comeback -> the lesson and a question to the viewer

reference.title: Why Are Dubai Locals So Rich? (It's Not Oil)

shapes.name: Pick one (the viewer chooses, then the reveal)
shapes.when: two or three money paths a viewer can choose between, where the one that looks worse wins (take $40M in salary or own a small insurer; $1M today or a penny doubled for 30 days)
shapes.beats: hook: 'Which one would you pick?' with the options side by side, each a thing on screen -> a one-second pause to choose -> each option plays out in turn with its number counting up -> the reveal: the quiet option wins, slammed in -> why, in one line -> loop: 'still picking the first one?'

reference.title: Who Would You Choose To Become a Billionaire Overnight?

shapes.origin: research 2026-11-05: market data (23 s, 1,954 views an hour); arrangement read from the title and length, not watched frame by frame

shapes.name: The hidden payer
shapes.when: how a famous company really earns, told as one hidden payer behind the obvious product; fits airlines, stadiums and stores whose money comes from a partner
shapes.beats: hook: the business everyone knows and the thing it obviously sells -> what that brings in, a sourced figure -> how little is left after costs -> the asker: so where is the money? -> the payer nobody sees, a sourced figure, money flying in -> the turn: that payer outweighs the whole profit -> payoff: who really pays, a question back to the viewer

shapes.name: The advert is the show
shapes.when: a famous creator or brand whose show is marketing and whose money comes from a plain product; fits YouTubers, sports teams, celebrity brands
shapes.beats: hook: the famous thing everyone thinks makes the money, denied -> that famous thing loses money, a sourced figure -> the asker: so where does the money come from? -> the ordinary product on a shelf, its sales -> its profit and margin -> the turn: the famous thing is only the advert for the product -> payoff: what the whole business is worth, a question back to the viewer

shapes.name: The exit door
shapes.when: a tax, fee or rule aimed at the very rich whose surprise is that the rich can step out of its reach; fits wealth taxes, exit taxes, residency rules
shapes.beats: hook: the easy-money belief denied -> the bill on paper, a sourced figure -> one example fortune's bill, computed -> the asker: so they just pay? -> where the money really is (shares, not cash) -> the turn: the people it was meant for simply leave first -> payoff: what happened to the bill, a question back to the viewer

shapes.name: The war chest
shapes.when: a famous fortune that looks idle but is working and waiting; fits Berkshire's cash, a company's buyback chest, a sovereign fund
shapes.beats: hook: the giant idle pile and the belief that it's wasted, denied -> its size made physical -> where it really sits and what it quietly earns -> the open question: why keep it so big? -> the turn: the sale it is waiting for -> payoff: the pile is a weapon, not a waste -> loop

shapes.name: The small paycheck
shapes.when: a billionaire whose paycheck is tiny because the fortune is a stake the company can't pay him; fits Bezos, Zuckerberg, Buffett
shapes.beats: hook: the famous name's tiny salary next to a bigger cost the company pays for them -> the asker: why so small? -> a comparison salary (another boss's) -> where the real money is (a stake) -> its size, sourced -> the turn: how many years of salary it equals -> payoff: the cost against the salary, and paycheck or shares?

shapes.name: The receipt
shapes.when: a famous subscription business whose giant totals become one member's yearly receipt; fits Netflix, Spotify, gyms, Amazon Prime
shapes.beats: hook: the giant spend and what is still kept -> promise: where does that much come from? -> the payers counted -> one person's year of payments -> what part buys the product -> the turn: the side money everyone assumes is big is tiny -> payoff: what is kept from each person, and a question

shapes.name: The zoom-in
shapes.when: a famous total too big to picture, made real by dividing it down to one night and one person; fits tours, stadiums, launches, sales days
shapes.beats: hook: the giant total with the famous name, as one striking rate -> promise: how can it be that much? -> how the money is really made, one step a beat (who pays, for what, the rule behind it) -> the turn: the part people miss (what the total is NOT, or who really pays) -> payoff: the most surprising slice, and a question. One time rate at most: never the same total per hour, per day, per year
shapes.revised: 2026-11-14: owner note on v-20261114-03, the unit ladder (minute, hour, day, year) gave the viewer nothing they didn't know

shapes.name: Who holds the ledger
shapes.when: one giant debt explained by following who it is owed to, ending on what it means per person
shapes.beats: hook: the giant total and its twist -> how fast it grows -> who holds most of it -> the turn: who holds the rest -> split over every person -> payoff figure and a question that loops to the hook

shapes.name: The cycle
shapes.when: a what-if whose answer is that nature runs it on a timetable: the story is a cycle, not a single change
shapes.beats: hook: the what-if about a place -> it already happened, again and again -> what drives it on the map -> what the place looked like last time -> the catch: who far away would feel it -> payoff: when it comes round again -> loop

shapes.name: The domino
shapes.when: a what-if whose consequences spread outward place by place from one point on the map, told as a day counter
shapes.beats: hook: one place on the map shuts -> the scale of what passes it -> day by day, one place after another feels it, each on the map -> the twist (the one who could shut it needs it too) -> the payoff -> loop

shapes.name: The drift
shapes.when: a why-placed story whose answer is something drifting one way across the map (wind, smoke, water) and people sorting themselves by it
shapes.beats: hook: the city map split, rich on one side, poor on the other, and the question why -> the invisible force drawn on the map (wind arrows) -> what it carried, spreading across the map place by place -> who moved away from it, the map recolouring -> the turn: the cause is gone, the split stays -> the payoff figure -> loop

shapes.name: The meltdown
shapes.when: a what-if where one thing vanishing at one spot redraws coastlines far away, followed from space
shapes.beats: hook: one huge thing on the map disappears -> seen from space, how big it is -> where its water goes -> one low place after another under the new sea, each on the map -> the turn: the place itself changes too -> the payoff: the one figure behind it all -> loop

shapes.name: The relay
shapes.when: a why-shaped story whose answer is one small move repeated across a map, each step handing on to the next, told as a race of boats east
shapes.beats: hook: the huge shape today and the question -> where it once ended, a line on the map -> who crossed it and what they were after -> the same step repeated, a colour spreading place by place across the map -> the turn: the people already living there -> payoff: how fast it reached the far coast -> loop back to the line it started from

shapes.name: The high ground
shapes.when: a why-shaped story whose answer is a border pushed back year by year until it sat on the mountains, painted and wrapped on the map
shapes.beats: hook: the hole in the big country and the question -> the hole's size against a place the viewer knows -> the fortress where it started -> the lowlands taken war by war, the border shrinking onto the mountains -> the turn: a call for protection freezes the line -> everything around it joins into one country, the island stays out -> payoff: how high even its lowest ground is -> loop back to the hole

shapes.name: The drain
shapes.when: a what-if where one thing running out at one spot on the map (a lake) pushes the world's ships onto a route thousands of kilometres longer
shapes.beats: hook: the shortcut on the map and the question -> it nearly happened, a figure the viewer can count -> where its water sits on the map and where every crossing spills it -> what fills it -> the rain stops: the lake shrinks step by step, the queues grow at both ends -> the turn: the long way round, drawn on the map -> payoff: how much of the world's sea trade rides on that rain -> loop

shapes.name: The assembly
shapes.when: a country that was once several pieces (or one that grew piece by piece): the map shows the pieces and joins them in the order history did
shapes.beats: hook: today's familiar outline cut into its old pieces and the question -> the pieces named and coloured, the first figure (how many) -> the first join: one piece swallows its neighbour on a date -> the joins speed up, each a date and a reason -> the last holdout and why it held out -> payoff: the most surprising date or fact (how recent it was) -> the finished outline snaps back to the first frame (loop)

reference.title: How Italy Became One Country, From 7 Pieces to 1 Kingdom

shapes.name: The patrol
shapes.when: a why-shaped story whose answer is one line on the map, followed end to end by a patrol truck as its kilometres count up
shapes.beats: hook: the line across the continent and the question -> how long it is against something the viewer can feel -> a truck starts driving it from one end, the counter climbing -> what lives on each side, shown on the map -> why it was built, the sheep in the south-east -> the turn: it used to be even longer -> payoff: what it really holds back -> loop back to the line
